item.title: SpaceX’s bid for Starship double catch thwarted, as booster ends up in ocean
item.description: SpaceX launched Starship towards orbit on Friday in its boldest test yet: a 22-hour flight that aimed to capture the entire rocket in a move meant to accelerate moon and Mars travel. But Elon Musk’s company had to lower its expectations when the first part of the double catch flopped. The first-stage booster malfunctioned and instead of returning to its Texas pad several minutes after lift-off, it ended up in the Gulf of Mexico after an automatic abort. item.title: Midterm losses could give Trump a quest to emerge from Apec summit as a winner
item.description: When G7 leaders gathered at the French resort of Evian-les-Bains in June, Donald Trump arrived late but wasted no time in grabbing the spotlight. With a cheeky declaration, “I am the boss”, the US president drew a ripple of awkward laughter from around the table. Months earlier, in his September 2025 address to the UN General Assembly, he told the gathering that “your countries are going to hell”. item.title: US flight departures resume after FAA lifts nationwide ground stop
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says airplane departures can resume after the agency lifted a nationwide ground stop caused by communications problems. Air travel across the United States had come to a halt earlier on Friday afternoon after the ordered all flights grounded because of a communications breakdown at the regional centres that manage the country’s air traffic. item.title: EU’s fixation on Chinese subsidies masks its own structural stagnation
item.description: The European Commission is moving to shield its industrial machinery and chemical sectors from Chinese imports, and is weighing a “kill switch” mechanism. Together with Washington, Brussels has settled into a familiar narrative: a record trade deficit with China is framed as proof of its “overcapacity” and attributed to state subsidies that allegedly tilt the global playing field.
